statement: You are given a singly linked list whose node values, read from head to tail, are listed in values. The tail's next pointer is set by cycleIndex: if cycleIndex is −1 the tail points to null, otherwise it points back to the node at 0-based position cycleIndex, forming a loop.
cycleIndex only describes how the list is built; the algorithm sees just the head and must discover a loop by following next pointers.
Return true if the list contains a loop, and false otherwise.

examples.explanation: The tail 5 links back to the node holding 2, so a slow pointer and a fast pointer moving through the list eventually land on the same node.
The tail points to null, so the fast pointer runs off the end and there is no loop.

constraints: The number of nodes is in the range [0, 10⁴]
cycleIndex is −1 or a valid index in the list
